blocks.prompt: 4. Reduce \(\sin^{4}\theta\) to an expression involving only function of multiples of \(\theta\), raised to the first power.
blocks.explanation:
This is Example 13 again, but for \(\sin^4\theta\) instead of \(\cos^4\theta\).
We must remove every power: the answer may contain \(\cos 2\theta\), \(\cos 4\theta\) but no squares.
Plan: use \(\sin^2\theta = \frac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{2}\), square, then use \(\cos^2 2\theta = \frac{1 + \cos 4\theta}{2}\).
steps:
Given: \(\sin^4\theta\).
To find: an equal expression in \(\cos 2\theta\), \(\cos 4\theta\) (first powers only).
Method: The power-reducing forms of \(\cos 2\theta = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta\) and \(\cos 4\theta = 2\cos^2 2\theta - 1\).

Square it
\[\sin^4\theta = \left(\dfrac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{2}\right)^2\]
\[= \dfrac{1 - 2\cos 2\theta + \cos^2 2\theta}{4}\]
Why: \((a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2\).

Reduce \(\cos^2 2\theta\)
\[\cos^2 2\theta = \dfrac{1 + \cos 4\theta}{2}\]
\[\sin^4\theta = \dfrac{1}{4}\left[1 - 2\cos 2\theta + \dfrac{1 + \cos 4\theta}{2}\right]\]
Why: From \(\cos 4\theta = 2\cos^2 2\theta - 1\), the double-angle formula with angle \(2\theta\).

Simplify
\[= \dfrac{1}{8}\left[2 - 4\cos 2\theta + 1 + \cos 4\theta\right]\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{8}\left[3 - 4\cos 2\theta + \cos 4\theta\right]\]
Why: Multiply the bracket by 2 and the \(\frac{1}{4}\) outside by \(\frac{1}{2}\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints this answer under the number "14." instead of "4.". The value \(\frac{3 - 4\cos 2\theta + \cos 4\theta}{8}\) is correct; only the label is wrong.
